verdict_reason: Strong multi-tenant scoping coverage, but the authoriseOrg path-vs-header mismatch guard is untested for DELETE - the one destructive verb - leaving a cross-tenant data-loss path with no test anywhere in the repo.

todos.issue: forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404 exercises the OperatorController.authoriseOrg mismatch guard for GET-by-id, list, PUT and POST but NOT DELETE - and no other test in the repo ever issues a DELETE where the path orgId differs from the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, so deleting authoriseOrg(orgId, sessionOrg) from OperatorController.delete would let org B soft-delete org A's address via A's path with the whole suite still green
todos.fix: Add a DELETE leg to forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404: perform delete(/organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{operator-id}, ORG_A, id).header(ORG_HEADER, ORG_B), expect 404, then assert the stored address is still AddressStatus.ACTIVE via repository.findById(id)

todos.issue: problemWithoutInstance strips an 'instance' key that this service never emits - GlobalExceptionHandler builds ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail and never calls setInstance, and it does not extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, so instance is null and omitted; the comment at line 229-231 claiming instance echoes the request URI is wrong for this codebase and the exclusion pre-weakens the byte-identical assertion against a future change that does populate instance
todos.fix: Drop problemWithoutInstance and compare the two parsed bodies directly, adding an explicit assertion that neither body contains an 'instance' key; if instance is later populated per-URI, reinstate the exclusion with a comment that matches the actual handler
